canonical_statement: The study aimed to identify post-AMI multimorbidity trajectories using explainable temporal machine-learning methods and assess their clinical, prognostic, and biological significance.
Eligible participants had incident acute myocardial infarction (ICD-10 I21), at least 5 years of follow-up or death within that window, no missing demographic data, and no implausible dates.

population.label: AMI eligibility criteria
inclusion_criteria: At least 5 years of follow-up or death within that window

canonical_statement: The retrospective cohort included 12,701 UK Biobank participants meeting the AMI inclusion criteria.

population.label: UK Biobank participants with incident acute myocardial infarction meeting study eligibility criteria

canonical_statement: Hospital inpatient ICD-10 diagnoses were filtered to remove pregnancy, perinatal, injury, nonspecific symptom, and transient infection codes; codes occurring fewer than 5 times were removed and remaining codes were truncated to 3 characters, yielding 1,008 distinct codes.
Diagnoses were split into a primary pre-AMI window from 365 to 1 day before AMI and a post-AMI window from 0 to 5 years after AMI.

Post-AMI diagnoses were represented as age-indexed binary matrices with ICD-10 codes as rows, integer ages from AMI to 5 years later as columns, 1 at first occurrence, and 0 otherwise; ages were standardized by mean-variance transformation.
Dynamic Time Warping k-means clustering was applied, and k=3 was selected after evaluating k=2 through 9 using elbow, silhouette, and Davies-Bouldin criteria.
Latent Dirichlet Allocation was applied independently within each DTW cluster using 2 topics per cluster to characterize co-occurring diagnostic themes.

Two independent clinicians grouped top ICD-10 codes into clinical categories for cluster labeling; inter-rater reliability was Cohen kappa 0.939 with 95% agreement across 60 codes and 4 minor disagreements.
Disease co-occurrence networks were constructed from Pearson correlations between binary code indicators, retaining edges above the 95th percentile and visualizing them in Cytoscape 3.10.

For supervised trajectory prediction, pre-AMI diagnoses were mapped to 27 ICD-10 clinical categories and combined with age, sex, BMI, and IMD score; logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost were tuned by 3-fold cross-validation using weighted F1, with inverse-frequency class weights and an 80/20 stratified train-test split.

A sensitivity analysis retrained and evaluated all classifiers using a restricted pre-AMI window from 365 to 7 days before AMI, excluding the final 7 days; AUC-ROC and weighted F1 confidence intervals used 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

Survival analysis fit four sequential Cox models: trajectory alone, SMART score alone, trajectory plus SMART, and a fully adjusted model adding age, sex, IMD, SBP, diabetes, prior CAD, cerebrovascular disease, and PAD; discrimination used Harrell C-index.

PheWAS mapped cluster conditions to PheCodes and tested UK Biobank genotyped SNP associations adjusted for age, sex, ancestry principal components, and genotyping array; FDR-significant SNPs were tested for Reactome pathway enrichment using a hypergeometric test with FDR correction.
Post-AMI multimorbidity trajectory membership was the multiclass prediction target for supervised learning.
Five-year all-cause mortality was evaluated as the survival outcome alongside the SMART risk score.
Among the 12,701 eligible participants, the reported median age at AMI was 69 years (IQR 63-74) and 30.9% were male.

canonical_statement: The authors propose that provisional trajectory labels at AMI could support trajectory-specific care pathways alongside SMART scoring, but state that diverse-population validation and prospective implementation studies are required before clinical deployment.

UK Biobank healthy-participant selection bias may underestimate the prevalence and complexity of multimorbidity trajectories and the predictive importance of deprivation-related features in real-world populations.
The cohort was predominantly White British, limiting generalisability.
Diagnoses were derived from hospital ICD-10 codes, missing primary-care conditions and sub-annual dynamics.
The observational design precludes causal inference.

The authors conclude that explainable temporal EHR modeling identifies three clinically interpretable and biologically grounded post-AMI multimorbidity trajectories that are predictable from pre-AMI data and complement existing clinical risk scores.
